articles.title: Local Golf Clubs Advance to Quarter-Finals of Manchester and District Alliance Competitions
articles.excerpt: Dukinfield, Rochdale, Brookdale and Denton golf clubs have reached the quarter-finals of the Manchester and District Golf Alliance Inter Club Knock Outs, showcasing local talent in regional competitions.
articles.content_html:
Four local golf clubs, Dukinfield, Rochdale, Brookdale, and Denton, have successfully advanced to the quarter-finals of the Manchester and District Golf Alliance Inter Club Knock Outs. This stage of the competition features teams from over 100 clubs across the region, highlighting the competitive spirit and skill present in local golf.

The Dunham Forest Trophy, a key event in the competition, consists of teams made up of a club professional and six leading amateurs. Notably, defending champions Ashton-on-Mersey were eliminated in earlier rounds, paving the way for other clubs to vie for the title. Dukinfield will be led by professional Dave Green as they host Leigh in their quarter-final match.

Other quarter-final matchups include Chorlton facing Dunham Forest, Heaton Moor against Wilpshire, and Wychwood Park taking on Disley. The final of the Dunham Forest Trophy is scheduled to take place at Dunham Forest Golf Club on September 26, 2026.

In addition to the knockout competitions, local clubs have been active in various medal and stableford events. Recent results from Ashton Golf Club saw Andy Lomas win his division after a card play-off, while Brookdale and Denton also reported strong performances in their respective competitions. These events not only foster community engagement but also encourage local talent to shine in the sport.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC Youth Team Begins Cup Campaign
articles.excerpt: Rochdale AFC's youth team has officially launched its cup campaign, aiming to showcase young talent in upcoming matches. The club is committed to developing players from the local community.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC's youth team has officially begun its cup campaign, as announced on August 18, 2026. The team will compete in a series of matches designed to highlight the skills and potential of its young players.

This initiative is part of Rochdale AFC's commitment to nurturing talent from within the community, providing competitive opportunities for young athletes.

Fixtures for the cup matches are expected to be announced shortly, and fans are encouraged to follow the team's progress as they aim for success in the tournament.

Further updates regarding match schedules and results will be available on the Rochdale AFC website.

articles.title: Plans Approved for 23 New Homes on Kirkholt Estate
articles.excerpt: Plans for a new 23-home apartment block and five terraced houses on the Kirkholt estate have been approved, aiming to provide affordable housing for local residents.
articles.content_html:
Plans for a new housing development on the Kirkholt estate in Rochdale have been approved, which will see the construction of a 23-home apartment block and five terraced houses off Queen’s Drive. The developer, Mosscare St Vincent Housing (MSV), aims to provide all homes for social rent, priced at approximately 60 per cent of market rates.

The site, which is currently vacant, previously housed an old block of flats that was demolished in 2009. Following its demolition, the land was briefly used by Kirkholt Medical Practice before the health centre relocated. The planning documents highlight the site as a prominent location within the local area, with the intention of creating a high-quality, sustainable development that addresses local housing needs.

MSV, a not-for-profit Registered Provider, manages nearly 9,000 homes across Greater Manchester, Lancashire, and West Yorkshire. The new apartments will consist of one-bedroom units, while the terraced houses will each have four bedrooms. The development is part of a broader strategy to reduce anti-social behaviour associated with the disused site and to enhance the community by providing affordable housing.

In addition to the housing, plans for a new community garden, to be managed by Q Gardens, have also been approved. This initiative aims to further support the local community and promote engagement among residents. The development is expected to contribute positively to the Kirkholt area by utilising vacant land and fostering a balanced community.

articles.title: Lift Out of Service at Derker Tram Stop Until Further Notice
articles.excerpt: The lift at Derker tram stop is currently out of service, affecting access for passengers. Alternative step-free routes are available for travel towards and away from Manchester.
articles.content_html:
The lift at Derker tram stop is out of service as of 16 August 2026, with no specified date for repairs. This disruption affects passengers using the tram service in both directions.

For those travelling towards Manchester, step-free access is available via a ramp from Cromford Street directly to the Manchester-bound platform. Passengers heading towards Rochdale can also use a ramp from Cromford Street and must cross the tracks to reach the Rochdale-bound platform.

Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has apologised for any inconvenience caused by this disruption and encourages passengers to plan their journeys accordingly.

Passengers are advised to check the TfGM website for live travel alerts for further updates regarding the lift's repair timeline.
